expectations.text: States that B2B org-owned workspaces have two consent surfaces, the end user's and an org admin's, not one.
expectations.evidence: "Your current design has one consent surface and one token type. You need two of each: Consent: the end user, plus a workspace admin who can gate installs."

expectations.text: Requires an admin approval gate (approval queue or admin-approved apps) designed as a first-class part of the scope and consent work rather than bolted on when the first enterprise customer asks.
expectations.evidence: Changes land in the scope taxonomy and consent steps; the skill says to build the admin surface up front, "not bolt it on when the first enterprise customer asks"; approval queue with policy modes is specified.

expectations.text: Includes org-wide grant review as part of the admin surface.
expectations.evidence: Admin tools: "List and revoke an app workspace-wide. List per-user grants. Re-approve when an app adds scopes."

expectations.text: Introduces an app-identity permission tier for the workspace bots, distinct from user-delegated permissions.
expectations.evidence: "Add a binding field to scope metadata: `delegated` or `app`"; "Design workspace bots as a separate principal".

expectations.text: States that app-identity / application permissions can only ever be consented by an admin, never by an end user.
expectations.evidence: "App-type scopes are admin-consent-only. A non-admin who clicks Allow can only file a request."

expectations.text: Notes the protocol core, token lifecycle, and consent-copy rules stay identical to the B2C case, so only the approval topology and the app-identity tier change.
expectations.evidence: It says "Neither change touches the protocol core: PKCE... refresh rotation... all stay as they are," but it also changes token lifecycle for bots and writes separate consent copy per type, and never says consent-copy rules stay identical.

expectations.text: States that over-scoping is a conversion risk at the admin gate, which the end user's approval cannot pass on the app's behalf.
expectations.evidence: No statement that over-scoping hurts conversion at the admin gate; it only covers the admin queue, unverified publishers limited to basic profile, and non-admins filing requests.

expectations.text: Binds each scope to a token type (bot/app identity versus user) rather than reusing one scope name across both undeclared.
expectations.evidence: "Add a binding field to scope metadata: `delegated` or `app`... Treat all existing scopes as `delegated`."

expectations.text: Warns that the same scope name means different things on a bot token and on a user token, so the binding must be decided per scope up front.
expectations.evidence: "Delegated: 'Read pages you can see.' App: 'Read all pages in the spaces you select.' These are not the same grant." Plus "Do this before the bots ship."
